questions.text: Tell me about a time you discovered a significant inventory discrepancy and how you resolved it.

key_points: How you detected it: cycle count, system alert, physical observation
Investigation method: location audit, transaction history review, team interviews
Root cause identified and corrective action taken
strong_answer_signals: Root cause fixed not just adjustment made
avoid: Made system adjustment without investigating cause

questions.text: Describe a time you improved inventory accuracy in a warehouse or DC.

key_points: Baseline accuracy level and how it was measured
Root causes identified: process gaps, scanning errors, receiving errors
Interventions and accuracy improvement achieved
avoid: Single fix for a multi-cause problem

questions.text: Tell me about a time you designed or overhauled a cycle count programme.

key_points: Previous programme shortcomings: frequency, coverage, ABC alignment
New design: ABC-based frequency, blind count methodology, threshold policy
Accuracy improvement and shrinkage reduction outcomes

questions.text: Tell me about a time you identified a process that was causing recurring inventory errors.

key_points: Pattern recognition: same error type, same location, same shift
Root cause analysis: 5-why or fishbone
Process change implemented and error rate reduction
strong_answer_signals: Quantified error rate before and after

questions.text: Describe a time you led a physical inventory count across a large facility.

key_points: Preparation: location labelling, system freeze, count team training
Execution: zone assignment, blind first count, recount process for variances
Reconciliation: variance investigation before system adjustment

questions.text: Tell me about a time you reduced shrinkage or stock loss in a warehouse operation.

key_points: Shrinkage type identified: theft, damage, admin error, vendor short-ship
Controls implemented: cage security, CCTV, receiving verification, process audit
Shrinkage value reduction achieved

questions.text: Describe a time you worked with operations to improve receiving accuracy.

key_points: Problem: short-ships or mis-picks from suppliers being booked in incorrectly
Solutions: blind receiving process, vendor scorecard, receiving SOP update
Receiving discrepancy rate improvement

questions.text: Tell me about a time you managed a WMS or ERP inventory module implementation or upgrade.

key_points: Pre-go-live: data cleanse, UAT, team training
Go-live: parallel run or phased rollout, issue triage
Post-go-live: accuracy stabilisation and process embedding
avoid: Big bang with no parallel run

questions.text: Describe how you built a culture of inventory accuracy accountability in a warehouse team.

key_points: Made accuracy visible: daily location accuracy scoreboard
Tied accuracy to team performance and recognition
Blameless investigation of errors as learning opportunities
avoid: Blame culture — drove hiding of errors

questions.text: Tell me about a time you reconciled a major discrepancy between the financial ledger and physical inventory.

key_points: Gathered transaction trail: receipts, issues, adjustments, transfers
Identified break: timing difference, unit of measure error, coding error
Corrected in both operational and financial system with documentation
strong_answer_signals: Both systems corrected and finance informed

questions.text: What is cycle counting and how does ABC classification determine count frequency?

key_points: Cycle count: continuous partial count vs annual full physical
ABC by value/velocity: A = weekly/daily, B = monthly, C = quarterly
Maintains perpetual accuracy without full operational shutdown

questions.text: How do you calculate and interpret inventory accuracy rate?

key_points: Locations accurate / total locations counted × 100
Measured at location-SKU level, not just aggregate value
Target: 99%+ for A-class; industry benchmark context
avoid: Value accuracy only — hides location errors

questions.text: What is a WMS adjustment audit and why is controlling system adjustments critical?

key_points: Adjustments change system stock without physical movement — can mask errors
Audit: every adjustment requires reason code, supervisor approval above threshold
Trend analysis of adjustments by type reveals systemic issues
avoid: Open adjustment access to all users

questions.text: How would you investigate a negative stock balance in the system?

key_points: Pull transaction history for that SKU-location
Common causes: pick before receipt posted, manual scan sequence error, unit of measure mismatch
Correct transaction at source, not just quantity adjustment
strong_answer_signals: Source correction not just stock fix
avoid: Assumed it was a system glitch

questions.text: How do you use transaction history reports in a WMS to investigate a stock discrepancy?

key_points: Filter by SKU, location, date range
Trace: receipt → put-away → pick → dispatch sequence
Identify missing or duplicate transaction, user, shift
strong_answer_signals: Named WMS systems used (SAP, Manhattan, HighJump)
avoid: Relied on memory or team self-report

questions.text: What is the difference between location accuracy and inventory value accuracy, and which matters more?

key_points: Location accuracy: right SKU, right quantity, right place — operational
Value accuracy: financial book vs physical value — financial reporting
Both matter: location for operations, value for finance — root cause often same
avoid: One is always more important without context

questions.text: How do you manage first-in-first-out (FIFO) compliance in a warehouse and why does it matter?

key_points: WMS directed put-away and pick by receipt date
Physical: date rotation labelling, location discipline
Matters: expiry management, quality, financial FIFO costing
avoid: Manual FIFO with no system support

questions.text: How do you handle inventory adjustments for damaged goods found during a cycle count?

key_points: Segregate and quarantine damaged stock immediately
Grade damage: rework, return to vendor, write-off, discount sale
System adjustment with reason code and supporting photo/documentation

questions.text: How would you design a variance threshold policy for inventory adjustments?

key_points: Threshold tiers by value: auto-approve low value, manager approval mid, director for high
Reason code mandatory for all adjustments regardless of value
Monthly threshold breach reporting to finance and ops leadership

questions.text: What KPIs would you track as an inventory control analyst and at what frequency?

key_points: Daily: location accuracy %, cycle count completion rate, open discrepancies
Weekly: adjustment value by reason code, shrinkage by type
Monthly: accuracy trend vs target, write-off value, vendor discrepancy rate
avoid: Monthly only — too infrequent for operational control

questions.text: You count a location and find 50 units in the system but only 35 physically. What steps do you take before making any system adjustment?

key_points: Recount the location to rule out count error
Check adjacent locations for mis-slotted stock
Review transaction history for recent picks, moves, or receipts on that SKU

questions.text: During a cycle count programme review you notice one shift consistently has higher discrepancy rates than others. How do you handle it?

key_points: Validate the pattern with at least 4 weeks of data
Investigate: process adherence, training, equipment, supervisor oversight
Raise with operations management with evidence; propose targeted intervention

questions.text: Finance requires a year-end physical inventory count to be completed in one weekend. How do you plan and execute it?

key_points: Pre-count: system freeze, location clean-up, count team briefing, zone assignment
Count day: blind first count, immediate recount for variances above threshold
Post-count: variance investigation before cut-off, finance sign-off

questions.text: A warehouse operative tells you they think a colleague has been stealing product. How do you respond?

key_points: Take the report seriously and document it immediately
Escalate to HR and security — do not investigate alone
Review inventory records for that area/shift to see if data supports concern
strong_answer_signals: Immediate escalation to HR and security
Did not accuse or confront individually
avoid: Shared the allegation with other team members

questions.text: Your WMS goes down mid-cycle count. How do you manage?

key_points: Switch to paper count sheets — pre-printed from last system backup
Track all movements manually during downtime with timestamp
On system recovery: enter manual counts, reconcile with any movements during outage
avoid: Resumed count without accounting for movements during outage

questions.text: A supplier is consistently short-shipping by 2-5% and your team has been booking in full quantities. How do you fix this?

key_points: Quantify total value of over-booked stock over past 6 months
Implement blind receiving immediately — count before system booking
Formal supplier dispute raised via procurement with evidence
strong_answer_signals: Procurement engaged for formal dispute and credit
avoid: Accepted going forward without recovering past loss

questions.text: Operations wants to skip cycle counts during peak season to focus on throughput. How do you respond?

key_points: Explain the risk: accuracy drops during high-volume periods — errors multiply faster
Propose a reduced but maintained count plan: A-class only during peak
Quantify past cost of post-peak accuracy recovery

questions.text: What draws you to inventory control specifically rather than other supply chain roles?

key_points: Precision and process discipline appeal
Tangible impact: accuracy drives service and financial integrity
Detective-like investigation of discrepancies
strong_answer_signals: Specific to control not just supply chain
Operational precision as a genuine strength
avoid: No specific aspect of control articulated

questions.text: How do you stay motivated when much of your work is routine counting and data reconciliation?

key_points: See the bigger picture: accuracy underpins service and P&L
Find the detective work in discrepancy investigation engaging
Set personal improvement targets and measure progress
avoid: No coping mechanism or genuine engagement

questions.text: Where do you see inventory control technology heading in the next few years?

key_points: RFID and autonomous mobile robots (AMRs) for continuous cycle counting
Computer vision for real-time location accuracy monitoring
AI-driven anomaly detection replacing rule-based adjustment audits
strong_answer_signals: Realistic timeline and current adoption context

questions.text: How do you build and maintain a high-accuracy inventory control team?

key_points: Hire for precision, process orientation, and curiosity
Daily accuracy scoreboards and team huddles
Blameless error investigation culture with SOP improvement as outcome

questions.text: How do you influence warehouse operations managers to prioritise inventory accuracy?

key_points: Translate accuracy to operational cost: rework, re-picks, customer returns
Share accuracy data in their weekly ops review not just your own
Celebrate shared wins when accuracy improves
avoid: Presented only in inventory control meetings

questions.text: Tell me about a time you managed a cross-functional project to reduce inventory write-offs.

key_points: Write-off root cause analysis across procurement, operations, and finance
Cross-functional action plan with owners and deadlines
Write-off value reduction achieved and sustained

questions.text: How do you ensure unit of measure accuracy when receiving goods into the WMS?

key_points: UOM defined on item master and matched to PO
Receiving staff trained on each vs case vs pallet receiving
UOM errors flagged as root cause category in discrepancy analysis
strong_answer_signals: UOM as tracked discrepancy root cause
avoid: Treated all discrepancies the same without UOM category

questions.text: What controls would you put in place to manage inventory in a bonded or customs warehouse?

key_points: Strict goods-in and goods-out documentation with customs references
Segregated physical locations for bonded stock with access controls
Regular reconciliation of customs declarations vs system stock

questions.text: Tell me about a time you trained warehouse staff on inventory accuracy procedures.

key_points: Assessed training gap: new SOP, new system, new hires
Training design: hands-on, location-based, competency sign-off
Accuracy improvement post-training and knowledge retention checks
avoid: Slideshow only with no practical element

questions.text: Describe a time you introduced a new inventory control process that faced resistance from the warehouse team.

key_points: Understood source of resistance: extra work, distrust, unclear benefit
Involved team in design and piloted with willing participants first
Demonstrated benefit with data; rolled out with team champions
